title: Beyond computable change bounds

based_on.title: Turing Degrees And The Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: Section 2.1, printed p.2, Definition 2.3 for the computable-bound convention; the pointwise simulator and diagonal construction are developed explicitly here

summary: Construct a limit-computable set with no computably bounded-change presentation, separating finite changes on each input from a computable allowance for them.
abstract: A computable membership guess can eventually settle on every input while giving no computable estimate of how many times it will change. Allowing an input-dependent computable allowance already goes beyond every fixed finite allowance, but it still misses some limit-computable sets. To see this, number all proposed approximation programs together with programs proposing their bounds. Each pair can be turned into a convergent sequence of binary guesses, even when the proposed bound program is partial. Reversing the eventual answer of each candidate at its own index then produces a limit-computable set that no computably bounded presentation can describe. Its guesses change finitely often on every input, yet no total computable function bounds those counts, and replacing the approximation cannot repair that obstruction.
